term: "Broad Learning System"

## Simple explanation

A Broad Learning System (BLS) is a learning architecture that adds groups
of feature and enhancement nodes side by side, rather than building a
deeper stack of layers. Some versions can update the output solution
incrementally when nodes are added.

## Technical explanation

The original BLS constructs mapped feature nodes and nonlinear enhancement
nodes, combines their outputs, and solves for output weights using a
closed-form or incremental method. The method is associated with
randomized mappings and ridge-regression-style solutions; implementation
details vary across adaptations.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

BLS is an alternative architecture for settings where incremental
expansion or fast retraining is useful. Engineers should compare its
accuracy, memory use, stability, and update cost with established
architectures on the target data rather than assuming it is universally
faster or more accurate.

## How it works

Input data is transformed into feature nodes, which are then combined with
enhancement nodes. The resulting design matrix is used to calculate output
weights. Additional nodes may be incorporated and the output solution
updated without training a conventional deep stack from scratch.

## Practical example

A researcher can test a BLS on a tabular classification task by mapping
input features into node groups, fitting an output layer, and measuring
held-out performance against simpler baselines.

## Common misconceptions

- "Broad" does not mean the model has no hidden computations or parameters.
- Incremental updates do not remove the need for validation and resource
  measurement.
- BLS is not the same architecture as a conventional deep neural network.
